title: Breaking timescales with generative sampling of conformational transitions.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links. Listed the full file tree of the official GitHub repo (Tangcyu/Gen-COMPAS) via the GitHub API and read its README: the only data is one demo trajectory for the Trp-cage miniprotein (0th.Iteration.noh.dcd, 22.6 MB binary coordinate file) plus NAMD (a molecular dynamics engine) input and force-field files. Searched Zenodo for Gen-COMPAS: no matching deposit. Did not download the DCD.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the method was applied to systems from a miniprotein to a pentameric ligand-gated ion channel, and that committors, transition states and free-energy landscapes were recovered (abstract only; Nature full text is paywalled and not in Europe PMC).

a1_downloadable.note: Code and one demo trajectory are on GitHub (checked the file tree). No deposit of trajectories for the other systems was found on Zenodo; the paper's data statement was not readable (paywalled).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked the repo: there is no label table. The committor (probability a structure reaches the end state before the start state) is not a column anywhere; it would have to be computed by running simulations and training a committor network on raw coordinate trajectories.

a3_inputs_present.note: Atomic coordinates are present as a binary DCD trajectory with matching topology (PSF) for the Trp-cage demo; seen in the file listing, not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: No tabular measurements exist; trajectory coordinates are in angstroms by NAMD convention but there is no outcome quantity with units.

a5_enough_rows.note: The unit of generalisation is the molecular system: a handful of systems in the paper and only one (Trp-cage) in the repo. Frame count of the demo DCD not checked.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 22.6 MB demo; full workflow needs new MD simulations
a6_fits_laptop.note: Reproducing labels needs NAMD targeted and unbiased MD runs and diffusion-model training, which are GPU/cluster jobs for anything beyond the miniprotein.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: paper full text unavailable and the per-system trajectory data are not deposited where I could find them.

a8_label_provenance.note: Committor values here are outputs of a trained Variational Committor Network (a neural network) fitted to simulation frames, i.e. model predictions from simulated physics, not a physical measurement. Learning them would distil that model.

existing_models.name: Gen-COMPAS (this paper: diffusion model plus Variational Committor Network)
existing_models.score_and_split: Validated per system against long reference simulations (abstract only); no train/test split in the ML sense. Code open on GitHub (MIT-style LICENSE file present).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not read (paywalled); README warns that new systems need stepwise manual checking of generated structures and committor slices.

existing_models.name: Committor-guided rate estimation (JCTC 2024, arXiv 2408.05879)
existing_models.score_and_split: Neural committor via semigroup objective with adaptive sampling; evaluated on toy and small molecular systems (from search snippet).

existing_models.name: Graph neural network committor from atomic coordinates (arXiv 2507.17700)
existing_models.score_and_split: Geometric vector perceptron network predicting committor directly from coordinates (from search snippet); split not retrieved.

backbone.name: none suitable; per-system trajectory data, not a sequence/molecule/cell table
backbone.licence: Repo has a LICENSE file (1 KB, likely MIT; not opened)

honest_claim_h3: Any model would only reproduce committor-network outputs on one simulated miniprotein, which says nothing beyond that system.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use simulated protein structures to predict how likely each one is to finish a shape change rather than revert.
plain_idea.train_on: Frames from molecular dynamics simulations of one small protein (Trp-cage) with atomic coordinates; number of frames unknown (not opened).
plain_idea.predict: The committor, the probability a structure goes on to the end shape first; here it comes from a trained neural network on simulations, not a lab measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Simulation groups studying protein folding and ion channels would get transition states cheaper, but that is the paper's own method, and the released data covers one system.

more_or_better_data.why: Only one demo system's trajectory (22.6 MB) is released, versus the paper's own multi-system results; no new data.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements or label table; committors are already probabilities produced by the paper's network.

models_beatable.why: Gen-COMPAS is a 2026 Nature method validated against reference simulations; beating it needs new MD on a cluster.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible new data measures the same quantity the same way and joins to this paper.

ml_idea: Rejected: train a committor predictor on released trajectories. Data is one demo trajectory, labels are network outputs, and producing more needs MD simulation on GPUs.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; generating committor labels requires running NAMD simulations and training the paper's networks, untimed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the repo for deposited per-system trajectories with committor values: done, only one demo DCD exists.

verdict_reason: Computational MD (molecular dynamics) method paper: no label table exists (A2), committors are neural-network outputs on simulations (A8), only one demo system is released (A5), and making more data needs GPU simulation (A6).
